title: Why Should the Children of a King
description: Why Should the Children of a King in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 144, headed “The witnessing and sealing Spirit, Rom. 8. 14 16. Eph. 1. 13 14”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Why should the child-ren of a King Go mourn-ing all their days? Great Com-fort-er, de-scend and bring Some to-kens of thy grace.

lines: Why should the children of a King
Dost thou not dwell in all the saints,
And seal the heirs of heaven?
When wilt thou banish my complaints,
Assure my conscience of her part
And bear thy witness with my heart,
That I am born of God.
Thou art the earnest of his love,
The pledge of joys to come;
And thy soft wings, celestial dove,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
